targets.outcome_quote: Our results suggest that the original findings of a facial feedback effect (Strack et al., 1988) and the null effect in the replication studies (Wagenmakers et al., 2016) are not contradictory: The facial-feedback effect was present when the camera was absent and participants were not concerned with performance monitoring; The effect diminished when the participants’ performance was recorded and participants were warned that their performance was being monitored.
